notes: Built from ep019.ts lines: only CAPITALS added; words identical to say. Owner rule 12 Nov: clear and unhurried, punch only on the key line.
persona: You are a clear, unhurried YouTube science narrator talking straight to one friend who is riding a falling space telescope. Conversational, warm and curious, an easy pace with short natural pauses between sentences, no audible breaths. Extra punch only on the key line of each beat. Words in CAPITALS get extra emphasis. Each line starts with a direction in parentheses: follow it, but never read the directions aloud.

lines.style: clear and gripping, a hushed shock
lines.tagged: You're riding a dying space TELESCOPE, falling at over twenty eight thousand kilometres an hour.
Every second, you fly almost EIGHT kilometres.
About a hundred and twenty kilometres up, you hit the first AIR.
It piles up in front of you. SQUEEZED air is the real heat.
At six hundred sixty degrees, aluminium MELTS. Your telescope starts to fall apart.

lines.style: the key line: big, clear punch
lines.tagged: Around seventy eight kilometres up, it BREAKS into pieces.

lines.style: calm and explanatory, a little relieved
lines.tagged: That's why astronauts ride home behind a HEAT shield.

lines.style: leaning in, amazed, sharing a true story
lines.tagged: This REALLY happened. On November fourth, NASA's Swift telescope came down.
It burned up over SUMATRA, in Indonesia, after almost twenty two years in space.

lines.style: warm and amused, a little grin
lines.tagged: Along the way, it caught over one thousand seven hundred fifty COSMIC explosions.
What should you survive next? The BEST comment becomes the next video.
